Package sc.fiji.snt.tracing.auto

Class TuftDetector

java.lang.Object
sc.fiji.snt.tracing.auto.TuftDetector
public class TuftDetector extends Object
Detects tufts (clusters of nearby terminal structure) in a Tree and reports them as ranked SeedPoints.

Four node populations can be scanned, selected via TuftDetector.Type:

  • TuftDetector.Type.TIPS: the tree's end points (DirectedWeightedGraph.getTips())
  • TuftDetector.Type.BRANCH_POINTS: the tree's branch points (DirectedWeightedGraph.getBPs())
  • TuftDetector.Type.TERMINAL_BRANCH_POINTS: branch points that are the immediate parent of at least one terminal branch, i.e., forks where twigs actually converge, as opposed to internal forks anywhere in the tree. More specific (and topologically more robust) than TuftDetector.Type.BRANCH_POINTS for tuft detection
  • TuftDetector.Type.TERMINAL_BRANCHES: the centroid of each terminal branch (a TreeStatistics.getBranches() segment with no children), i.e., the last unbranched run of nodes leading to a tip. Useful when tufts are formed by several short terminal twigs converging in one spot rather than by a single prominent tip/fork node. Because a discontiguous/beaded neurite can fragment into several short, spatially-close but topologically-unrelated terminal branches (mimicking a genuine tuft), short branches are down-weighted by default (see setPenalizeShortBranches(boolean))
  • TuftDetector.Type.BRANCH_DENSITY: every node of every branch, weighted by the arc length it locally represents. Measures the 'amount of neurite' in a neighborhood rather than a count of discrete tip/branch-point nodes, so it degrades gracefully under a discontiguous/beaded neurite instead of spiking (extra spurious tips) or dropping out (a lost branch point). Scans the whole tree, so a dense non-terminal trunk/shaft can also score as a hotspot
  • TuftDetector.Type.TERMINAL_BRANCH_DENSITY: as TuftDetector.Type.BRANCH_DENSITY, but restricted to terminal branches only keeping the measure focused on terminal structure like the other Types

A node's score is the (weighted) number of other nodes found within radius of it, optionally further weighted by thickness and/or intensity. Nodes belonging to the same tuft mutually reinforce each other's score, while isolated nodes score low. Candidates are then greedily suppressed by distance (highest score first) so that each tuft is reported once, at the location of its highest-scoring node.

Tiago Ferreira

    List<SeedPoint>
    detect(Tree tree, List<TuftDetector.Type> types)
    Detects tufts across several node populations in tree in a single pooled pass: candidates from every requested TuftDetector.Type are merged into one KDTree/scoring/suppression run, so a tuft that happens to show up in more than one (e.g. a fork sitting right next to a tip) is still reported once, rather than once per type.

      public TuftDetector(double radius)

      public void setWeightByThickness(boolean weightByThickness)
      Sets whether each node's thickness (PointInImage.radius, or its per-branch average for TuftDetector.Type.TERMINAL_BRANCHES) is added to its neighbor count when scoring. Default: true

    • setWeightByIntensity

      public void setWeightByIntensity(boolean weightByIntensity)
      Sets whether each node's sampled intensity (PointInImage.v, min-max normalized across the scanned population) is added to its neighbor count when scoring, in addition to (or instead of) thickness. Nodes with unassigned/NaN values contribute 0. Requires the tree to have been profiled beforehand (e.g. via PathProfiler#assignValues()); otherwise every node contributes 0 and this has no effect. Default: false

    • setPenalizeShortBranches

      public void setPenalizeShortBranches(boolean penalizeShortBranches)
      Sets whether short terminal branches have their contribution to the density score down-weighted, for TuftDetector.Type.TERMINAL_BRANCHES only. A discontiguous (e.g. beaded) neurite can fragment into several short, spatially-close but topologically-unrelated terminal branches, which would otherwise look like a genuine dense tuft. Weight is min(1, branchLength / radius), so branches at least as long as radius are unaffected. Default: true

    • setPercentileClip

      public void setPercentileClip(double percentileClip)
      Sets the robustness margin (0-45) for confidence normalization; see SeedConfidence.percentileClipNormalize(double[], double). Default: 10

    • detect

      Detects tufts across several node populations in tree in a single pooled pass: candidates from every requested TuftDetector.Type are merged into one KDTree/scoring/suppression run, so a tuft that happens to show up in more than one (e.g. a fork sitting right next to a tip) is still reported once, rather than once per type.
      Parameters:
      tree - the tree to scan
